purpose: Freeze graph-memory hard cases before taxonomy, ontology IR, materialization, or shadow retrieval work.

cases.title: Roster identity routing: party and NPC identity bundle
cases.current_risk: Roster-style questions may require identity bundles that span party members, NPCs, routes, and hubs rather than one lexical sentence match.
cases.why_graph_native: A graph can represent participants, aliases, route attachments, and hub relationships separately from the text that mentions them.
cases.future_graph_expectation: A future graph-expanded retrieval path should measure whether roster and hub identity links improve recall while keeping each candidate evidence item source-unit grounded.
must_preserve: source-grounded evidence only
no graph summary admitted as source evidence
no production retrieval behavior change in this rung
expected_future_trace: query asks for a roster or identity bundle
graph resolves relevant participant or route nodes
graph proposes linked source-unit candidates
candidate evidence remains source-unit grounded
cases.notes: Baseline definition only; this PR does not regenerate retrieval outputs or assert a complete roster.

cases.title: Clean control: preserve a known low-risk retrieval case
cases.current_risk: Graph expansion could add unnecessary context to a case that current retrieval already handles cleanly enough for baseline comparison.
cases.why_graph_native: A graph needs negative and control cases so expansion can be rejected when direct evidence is already sufficient.
cases.future_graph_expectation: Future graph work should show that graph-assisted paths do not degrade clean/control retrieval, citation grounding, or answer focus.
must_preserve: clean direct evidence remains preferred
no graph summary admitted as source evidence
no production retrieval behavior change in this rung
expected_future_trace: query has direct source-unit support
graph expansion is measured but not blindly admitted
irrelevant expanded candidates are rejected or ranked below direct evidence
cases.notes: This is a control-family baseline; future reports should attach real current-system outputs before promotion.

cases.title: Location hierarchy: Stonebridge / Rivers Edge Pub
cases.current_risk: Facts tied to a sublocation may not retrieve when the query names the parent location, or parent-location retrieval may over-attract unrelated sibling facts.
cases.why_graph_native: A graph can represent LOCATED_IN / CONTAINS_LOCATION separately from lexical route labels.
cases.future_graph_expectation: A graph-expanded retrieval path should connect Rivers Edge Pub evidence to Stonebridge queries without flooding unrelated Stonebridge context.
must_preserve: source-grounded evidence only
no graph summary admitted as source evidence
no production retrieval behavior change in this rung
expected_future_trace: query mentions parent location
graph resolves parent location node
graph traverses contained sublocation edge
candidate evidence remains source-unit grounded
cases.notes: Baseline definition only; this PR does not regenerate retrieval outputs.

cases.title: Alias identity bridge: Draven / necromancer role reference
cases.current_risk: Role, name, and alias-like references may fail to meet at retrieval time, while unsafe merging could collapse distinct entities without source support.
cases.why_graph_native: A graph can model alias candidates, role labels, and identity links with provenance and lifecycle state instead of treating every shared label as a merge.
cases.future_graph_expectation: Future graph work should measure whether name/role bridges improve recall while preserving merge caution and source-grounded traceability.
must_preserve: no unsafe entity merge
source-grounded evidence only
no graph summary admitted as source evidence
expected_future_trace: query mentions a role or name variant
graph evaluates candidate identity or alias edge
edge provenance and lifecycle state are visible
candidate evidence remains source-unit grounded
cases.notes: The case names the intended bridge focus; it does not assert a confirmed alias beyond existing source-backed artifacts.

cases.title: Session-scoped final beat recall
cases.current_risk: Questions such as the last thing that happened in a session may need session-bound ordering rather than topical similarity alone.
cases.why_graph_native: A graph can represent session membership, sequence, and final-beat candidate relationships separately from lexical overlap.
cases.future_graph_expectation: Future graph work should measure whether session-scoped ordering improves final-beat retrieval without pulling in neighboring-session events.
must_preserve: session scope remains explicit
source-grounded evidence only
no production retrieval behavior change in this rung
expected_future_trace: query asks for the final beat of a session
graph resolves the session node
graph evaluates ordered source units or session-memory records
candidate evidence remains source-unit grounded
cases.notes: Baseline definition only; future comparisons should attach measured outputs for the exact session artifacts used.

cases.title: Breadcrumb natural-language query over session-memory records
cases.current_risk: Natural-language questions over breadcrumbed or session-memory records may miss relevant context when query terms differ from normalized breadcrumb labels.
cases.why_graph_native: A graph can connect normalized breadcrumbs, routes, source units, and session-memory records while preserving the original evidence anchors.
cases.future_graph_expectation: Future graph work should measure whether breadcrumb-to-route relationships improve natural-query recall without overriding source-grounded citations.
must_preserve: breadcrumb normalization does not become source evidence
source-grounded evidence only
no production retrieval behavior change in this rung
expected_future_trace: query uses natural language rather than exact breadcrumb labels
graph resolves related breadcrumb or route nodes
graph proposes source-backed records
candidate evidence remains source-unit grounded
cases.notes: Retained as a baseline family if session-memory breadcrumb records remain relevant; uncertain details should be clarified by later measured reports.

cases.title: Unresolved hook resurfacing through relationships
cases.current_risk: Unresolved hooks may not share lexical query terms with the later situation where they should resurface.
cases.why_graph_native: A graph can represent hook status, related entities, locations, threats, and sessions as traversable relationships with explicit source support.
cases.future_graph_expectation: Future graph reports should measure whether unresolved hooks can be surfaced as candidates through relationships without treating inferred relevance as source truth.
must_preserve: unresolved status remains explicit
inferred relevance is not source evidence
no production retrieval behavior change in this rung
expected_future_trace: query mentions a related entity, place, or threat
graph evaluates unresolved hook relationships
graph reports the path and source support
candidate evidence remains source-unit grounded
cases.notes: Baseline definition only; no unresolved-hook registry is introduced in this PR.

cases.title: High-degree hub over-attraction control
cases.current_risk: Broad hubs may connect to many records and flood retrieval context when graph expansion treats every edge as equally useful.
cases.why_graph_native: A graph can expose node degree, edge type, and expansion path so broad hubs can be measured, capped, or rejected.
cases.future_graph_expectation: Future graph work should measure hub expansion cost and precision before any hub-driven retrieval path is promoted.
must_preserve: broad hub links do not override direct evidence
source-grounded evidence only
no production retrieval behavior change in this rung
expected_future_trace: query touches a broad hub
graph reports hub degree or expansion fan-out
graph caps or rejects low-value sibling candidates in shadow reports
candidate evidence remains source-unit grounded
cases.notes: This is a safety baseline for graph expansion; it does not define hub thresholds.

cases.title: Authority boundary: GM prep versus played truth
cases.current_risk: Prep notes, rumors, candidate facts, and played events can be conflated unless authority state and evidence role are explicit.
cases.why_graph_native: A graph can keep authority state, visibility state, evidence role, and source references attached to nodes or edges instead of flattening them into one truth bucket.
cases.future_graph_expectation: Future graph work should measure whether authority boundaries remain visible and prevent unsafe promotion of prep or rumor into played canon.
must_preserve: played, prep, rumor, candidate, and source-supported states remain distinguishable
no graph summary admitted as source evidence
no production retrieval behavior change in this rung
expected_future_trace: query touches facts with different authority states
graph reports authority and evidence roles
graph prevents unsupported promotion in shadow output
candidate evidence remains source-unit grounded
cases.notes: This case defines an authority-boundary evaluation need; taxonomy values arrive in a later rung.

cases.title: Citation grounding: graph summaries are never source evidence
cases.current_risk: Graph reports, summaries, or derived nodes could be mistakenly cited as source evidence instead of the underlying source units.
cases.why_graph_native: A graph can distinguish derived summaries and relationships from source anchors, but validators must enforce that distinction.
cases.future_graph_expectation: Future graph reports and retrieval traces must cite source artifacts for evidence and treat graph summaries only as navigation or diagnostic aids.
must_preserve: no graph summary admitted as source evidence
citations point to source artifacts or source units
no production retrieval behavior change in this rung
expected_future_trace: query is expanded through graph-derived structure
graph report identifies derived nodes separately from source anchors
answer evidence cites only source-backed artifacts
graph summary remains diagnostic rather than evidentiary
cases.notes: This baseline case is a promotion gate for all later graph reports and shadow retrieval work.
